method: Commons API search (filemime:audio) and category browsing (Sounds of level crossing signals, Sounds of rail transport, Short-duration soundscapes, Ambient sounds, Audio files of doorbells, Audio files by Gravity Sound, LaSonotheque.org). Licences read from extmetadata. Decoded with ffmpeg only; trimmed, DC removed and peak-normalised in numpy; checked visually by waveform and spectrogram, plus video frames for S4. Nothing was synthesised.
download_note: upload.wikimedia.org answered HTTP 429 (Retry-After 600) for original files throughout the session, probably because other swarm units share the address. All audio was therefore fetched as Commons' own transcodes (MP3, Ogg or VP9 WebM) of the originals. They are the same recordings, re-encoded lossily by Wikimedia. file_url gives the original and downloaded_url the transcode actually fetched. Total downloaded about 17 MB.

items.title: Glockenschlagwerk Bahnhof Fridingen.ogg
items.author: Olga Ernst
items.onset_note: first strike transient (2 ms envelope, threshold 25% of peak, walked back to the attack start)
items.format: WAV PCM s16, 44100 Hz, stereo (mono sources duplicated), DC removed, peak-normalised to -3 dBFS
items.what_it_shows: A mechanical bell striker (Glockenschlagwerk) at Fridingen station, Baden-Württemberg, Germany, recorded on site; the file is a run of 13 separate strikes about 0.9 s apart. One isolated strike (source 6.85-8.05 s, strike at about 7.0 s) is cut out with its natural decay to near silence.
items.verified_date_or_place: 2019-04-20 (Commons DateTimeOriginal; category 'April 2019 in Baden-Württemberg'); Bahnhof Fridingen (an der Donau), Germany, per title. Categorised as a level-crossing bell, so it is a railway signal bell at a station, not a hand-rung platform bell.
items.used_as: S1 bell, one strike. Same file used at every placement: Beat A 33.6 s, Beat B 47.6 s, ledger card 49.9 s (pan left) and 52.4 s (pan right). Tag 'S1 · station bell, Fridingen, 20 Apr 2019 · recorded elsewhere'.

items.notes: Downloaded as the Commons MP3 transcode of the Ogg original, because upload.wikimedia.org rate-limited (HTTP 429) downloads of originals during this session.
